newsitem.title: ITALY: Unlikely BOI aided lira at ERM start Monday-Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Unlikely BOI aided lira at ERM start Monday-Ciampi.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said he did not think the Bank of Italy had intervened on the lira on its first day of trading back in Europe's exchange rate mechanism.

Ciampi, asked in an interview with daily La Stampa if Italy would be able to sustain its new central parity of 990 lire per mark, replied "I think so. Take today (Monday). I don't believe the Bank of Italy intervened, yet we closed a bit above 990."
The lira rose to its highest level since October 7 in its first day of trade within the ERM on Monday. It touched 989.25 and spent much of the day near the 990 per mark central parity.
There was much market talk of Bank of Italy intervention in recent weeks selling lire to brake its rise to firmer ground beyond 1,000 ahead of expected lira ERM re-entry.

Ciampi told La Stampa recent lira prices had been influenced by Bank of Italy actions "only because it needed on one side to rebuild its reserves and on the other rebalance the alteration in the exchange rate caused by high short term interest rates, needed to reduce inflation."
